summary.intent: Improve system diagrams in a cross-product design doc, then update a memory loop rollout design doc to align with a new RFD that moves CheckpointAnalysis generation to the entire.io API, and address adversarial review findings.
summary.outcome: Updated two System Diagrams sections in the cross-product design doc and performed two full adversarial review + fix cycles on the memory loop rollout spec, addressing tenant isolation, cache invalidation, degraded-mode safety, unsynced checkpoint handling, and authorization contract gaps.

repo: The memory loop rollout spec lives at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-memory-loop-rollout-design.md, distinct from earlier phased design docs under docs/plans/
RFD-014 (github.com/entirehq/company-knowledge/pull/76) moves CheckpointAnalysis generation from the CLI to the entire.io API, with local insights DB becoming a cache layer
The cross-product design doc (2026-04-08-session-analysis-cross-product-design.md) has a dedicated 'System Diagrams' section with Current World and Proposed Design subsections
Agent memories were intentionally excluded from the Current World diagram
The memory loop spec had open Q1/Q2 questions about shared repo backend that were intentionally left unchanged

code.finding: Storage section originally had no cache schema for CheckpointAnalysis; added analysis_cache table with checkpoint_id, repo_id, content_hash, schema_version, generator_version, processed_at, fetched_at, source fields
Generation pipeline originally only handled synced checkpoints via API fetch; unsynced checkpoints had no documented path — fixed by adding explicit upload-for-on-demand-analysis flow

Authorization contract relied on caller-supplied repo/checkpoint IDs with only echo-back validation; fixed to require server-side repo membership enforcement, opaque identifiers, and explicit rejection of mismatched responses

Cache invalidation originally tracked content_hash and fetched_at only; added generator_version field so cache is invalidated when local generation semantics change even if analysis JSON is byte-identical

Degraded-mode fallback originally allowed memory creation/update/reactivation from arbitrarily stale cache; fixed to make stale entries (>48h) skip-only during outages, with full-outage refresh completing with zero generation and a prominent warning

workflow: The /codex:adversarial-review skill runs a challenge review questioning design choices and assumptions, not just implementation defects — useful for catching trust boundary and degradation failures in design docs
The Codex review verdict 'needs-attention' with 'no-ship' reasoning surfaced two rounds of high/medium findings that were then addressed in-session
Interactive playgrounds (HTML with SVG) were created alongside markdown diagram improvements as a companion visualization tool
The security hook flagged innerHTML usage in the HTML playground, requiring a rewrite to safe DOM methods (textContent)

friction: Initial broad diagram improvement to the markdown file was rejected by the user — had to undo all changes and redo only the two System Diagrams sections
The user interrupted an in-progress operation after the undo request, requiring re-reading the file to understand current state
The Proposed Design diagram had a conceptual error (CLI and Website connected to each other) that required a correction pass based on user screenshot feedback
The security hook blocked the first version of the HTML playground due to innerHTML usage, requiring a full rewrite
open_items: Open Q1/Q2 in the memory loop rollout spec about shared repo backend were intentionally left unchanged
The note about future server-side memory generation possibility was added but not scoped or scheduled
The PR rollout sequence (PR 1-5) was updated for PR 3 but may need further review as the API infrastructure comes online
The CLI search worker (wrangler.search.jsonc) requires manual deploy and is not covered by main CI — routes 404 until manually deployed
